item.description:

Authors: Yu-Fei Liu, Jinchen Liu, Tiema Qian, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental protocol to identify antisymmetric Hall responses in quantum materials, relevant to Berry curvature studies.

Tags: #experiment #method #transport

Abstract: Rapid advances in nonlinear Hall transport provide new probes of quantum geometry, but transverse signals generally mix Hall and non-Hall contributions that are difficult to disentangle. Here, the authors introduce a unified experimental protocol that exchanges current and voltage directions to identify antisymmetric Hall and symmetric non-Hall responses. Measurements across representative quantum materials validate the method in both linear and nonlinear regimes.

item.title: [7] Spin-density wave of ferrimagnetic building blocks masking the ferromagnetic quantum critical point in NbFe2
item.description:
Last authors: A. Neubauer, C. Pfleiderer, F. M. Grosche, and P. G. Niklowitz

Authors: T. Poulis, G. Mani, J. Sturt, W. J. Duncan, H. Thoma, V. Hutanu, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering study on magnetic order near a quantum critical point.

Tags: #neutron_scattering #magnetism

Abstract: Ferromagnetic quantum critical points can be masked by emerging modulated magnetic order. Here, the authors use neutron diffraction to show that the example of NbFe 2 provides the first case, where the masking modulated order is a longitudinal spin-density wave. The latter has a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment and is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets. The findings can serve as a test case for magnetic quantum order-by-disorder models.
